card.name: Small words before a missing verb
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as 'to', 'not' and 'and/or' right where a verb is expected next, as in 'not enough data points to' or 'could not'. Also fires on odd partway-through-name pieces in citations.

modes.label: Linking word before verb
modes.description: 'to', 'not' or 'and/or' sits just before a verb like plot, be assessed or modify.
modes.example: Sorry, there are not enough data points<< to>> plot this chart.

modes.label: Inside author names
modes.description: Partway through a surname in a reference list.
modes.example: Loberg, M.D., Buddem<<eyer>>, E.V.: Application of pharmacokin

modes.label: Could not in trial text
modes.description: The word 'not' after 'could' in a statement about what was not assessed.
modes.example: beyond 24 weeks could<< not>> be assessed.

card.writes: It seems to weaken Chinese verb-phrase starters and push toward English -ing words like dressing and tasting.
card.plain: It marks small words like 'to' or 'not' that come just before a verb, plus some pieces of author names.
